blindSummary: 2024 facility ban expanded in 2026 to colleges and universities; part of an 18-member group of states/provinces with statutory birth-sex definitions. This state/province's statutes are catalogued in a July 2026 independent legal-risk assessment map of state/province anti-trans law.
blindSourceSummaries: An independent travel-safety outlet's July 2026 anti-trans legal-risk assessment map (republished 27 Aug 2026 by a regional LGBTQ site): per state/province legal-risk grading; this state/province's entry reflects the 2026 expansion of its bathroom ban to colleges and universities, within a national frame of severe policies in effect.

A statement by the state/province civil-liberties union after the governor signed a 2026 law: it requires transgender students in public schools and universities to use restrooms and changing facilities that do not match their gender. The union's executive director - the national union's first openly transgender affiliate leader - condemns the law as treating trans youth as outcasts and notes lawmakers rejected single-user-stall alternatives framed as privacy fixes.
